newsitem.title: UK: UK corporate sector to see takeover surfeit - report.
newsitem.headline: UK corporate sector to see takeover surfeit - report.

text.p: Britain's corporate sector is expected to witness a surfeit of takeovers in the coming weeks as financiers reactivate deals put on hold during the election campaign, the Guardian reported on Friday.
The newspaper said at least two big takeovers may break as early as Monday.

"Speculation centres on the financial sector, where analysts and professional investors are convinced that a wholesale realignment of banks, building societies and insurance groups is due," the Guardian said.
The newspaper said several financiers had indicated they were preparing for their busiest six-month period in memory.
"With the elections now out of the way, the fingers will go back on the button," a financier told the Guardian.
The newpaper said analysts were convinced B.A.T Industries would resurrect plans to demerge its financial arm, including Allied Dunbar and Eagle Star, and merge it with another leading insurer.

A consolidation is also expected in the utilities sector with many financiers and big investors convinced that National Power or PowerGen could make a bid for the sole independent regional electricity firm Southern Electric, the Guardian said.
